**Readiness and slack** — what it takes to keep, reach and pay for capacities whose value lies in rare circumstances — readiness as response capability, slack and reconfiguration slack as different reserves, the resource threshold of a transition and its obstructions, and budget rules that remove options no one chose to give up (ADR-073). | [CLAIM-580](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-580.md) v2 | Transition threshold is stable under error | The assistant's own proposition, offered at the owner's invitation on 2026-11-05. The threshold of [CLAIM-571](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md) is the least, over admissible paths, of each path's peak requirement, and both the peak and the least move by at most the largest error in the requirement. So a planner who knows each configuration's cost to within ε knows a transition's threshold to within ε, and its reconfiguration slack to within 2ε. The error is also one-sided in a useful way: overestimating only raises the threshold, and underestimating anywhere can only lower it, possibly by opening a cheaper path that does not exist. It is the zero-dimensional case of the stability of sublevel-set persistence that Mirth et al. use. With several resources the same argument bounds the set of sufficient budgets coordinate by coordinate. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |

In A's branching model of assembly, the chance of reaching the target is a product of branch choices, each a ratio of the rates of the competing steps. If supply rises uniformly by λ, a step that consumes a further unit, binding another molecule, speeds up by λ, while a step within what is already assembled does not. So a choice is unchanged by abundance when its competing steps consume alike, and shifted when they differ. More of everything hurts where the wrong step consumes and the right one does not. Majikes et al. 2021 find exactly this for one fold of a DNA origami: two staple molecules can each take one end and block it, and the folded share j/(j + S₀) falls as staple excess rises. A's remark that "The relevant resource isn't always total abundance" is thus made exact. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |

| [CLAIM-878](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-878.md) v4 | Peak budgets favour provisional dispatch | A corollary of [CLAIM-577](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-577.md), found in running [LEAD-080](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-080.md)'s study ([CASE-315](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-315.md)). Under spend-matching the next budget is this period's peak, so a capability costing B* to mobilize stays affordable exactly as long as every period occupies capacity at that cost, as anything that mobilizes it does, and its first period with no such occupation loses it for good. If q_t is the chance that period t has nothing, the chance of losing it within n periods is 1 − ∏(1 − q_t). Whatever mobilizes counts: a use, a drill, a false alarm or a provisional dispatch ([TERM-109](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-109.md)) cancelled minutes later. So the dispatch policy decides how long the capability survives the rule. Sent provisionally to six reports a month, a heavy rescue squad is quiet in a month with chance e^(−6) and was still funded after nine years in 80 % of the study's runs; sent only on confirmation it was lost in every run within months. [CLAIM-561](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-561.md) says a high cancellation rate does not show waste; under this rule the cancellations are also what keeps the capability funded. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |

Competence k decays at rate δ and is rebuilt by maintenance bought from the budget above a holding cost h; the budget is a base B̄ plus η times observed use; and a capability is committed to an occasion only if k is at least k_lo. If the base alone sustains competence below k_lo, (β/δ)(B̄ − h) < k_lo, a capability that falls below k_lo is never committed, so never observed, so funded at the base, so never recovers. Funding maintenance apart from use at a level that sustains k_lo removes the state. In the study, at the same expected funding, the coupled rule lost the capability within thirty years in every run at one occasion in two and a half years and in 39 % at four a year, and the decoupled rule never did.
